pos.personaBrief: Ajax were described as very possession-oriented (Ballverliebt), built on ball rotation and recycling backward when no forward pass existed (La Grinta, These Football Times); Van Gaal said Milan play as Ajax play, wanting to win rather than hang back.

pro.personaBrief: Ajax were a possession team that did not hesitate to go long, with fast switches and long balls behind for running wingers (La Grinta, FourFourTwo), but they also circulated the ball patiently and the keeper started moves.

est.personaBrief: Roles were tied to the position, not the player, with wingers strictly on the touchline and the system above individuals (Ballverliebt, Planet Football), though players with the ball rotated and interchanged around it.

lar.personaBrief: Wingers hugging the touchline were fixed, mandatory roles (FourFourTwo, Rivaldo told to stay wide), with forward runs and quick switches of flank; crossing was reserved for the wingers.

blo.personaBrief: Ajax pressed immediately on losing the ball, hounding collectively with trained pressing packs, and played an extended team with few minutes in their own half (La Grinta, FourFourTwo, Planet Football).

mar.personaBrief: Defenders Reiziger, F. de Boer and Bogarde were classic man-markers with a libero (Blind), and midfielders tracked wide men; individual marking suited the stretched shape (Ballverliebt, La Grinta).

pla.personaBrief: Van Gaal imposed one philosophy and system whoever the opponent, and the individual had to subordinate to it; he arrived at Barcelona with an Ajax model, though he stated systems depend on players.

res.personaBrief: Attacking, conquering football that wants to win the game, not avoid defeat (his 1995 comment on Milan and PSG), with a pragmatic win-first attitude and late tweaks such as dropping Rijkaard back, while boasting of trophies won.

sis.personaBrief: The system was everything and the individual had to subordinate himself (Ballverliebt, Set Pieces); Rivaldo was benched, and he made Seedorf, Davids and others fit roles.

jog.personaBrief: He wanted physically strong, multifunctional, tactically intelligent players who can defend and attack, with big targets and small dribblers, while keeping a technical possession game.

bas.personaBrief: Ajax were built on academy players (13 of 18 in the 1995 final, average age 23, only two over 25, debuts for Seedorf, Davids, Melchiot) with very few signings, and youth gave results at once.

lid.personaBrief: Militaristic, dominant and rule-bound (Cruyff), with note-taking, strict ways of doing things, clashes with Brazilians, Stoichkov and Rivaldo, who was dropped and sent to the stands.
